A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BecomingLit and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The retained, added, and relocated material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-subject relighting and reenactment experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds shading ablations, measured runtime comparisons, and original Goliath-4 evaluation results.

M1.justification: The FLAME-conditioned Gaussian representation, diffuse network, analytical specular model, losses, and inference procedure are retained. Appendix A documents the same architecture despite the new U-Net terminology. PRT and spherical-Gaussian variants are experimental controls, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds actual training and evaluation on Goliath-4 subject QZX685, extending evaluation beyond the authors' capture dataset to an external light-stage dataset. v1 only described Goliath in Table 1. The original dataset evaluation and VFHQ/PolyHaven demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: The main RGCA and RGCA_FLAME baselines remain unchanged. Table 3 adds evaluated PRT-diffuse and spherical-Gaussian specular alternatives to the component comparisons. These are limited comparator additions rather than new complete avatar baselines.

E3.justification: The new Goliath evaluation introduces full-camera training with 10 held-out views and a restricted configuration with 16 training and 4 evaluation cameras, using the provided expression split and holding out 10% of lighting patterns. A new runtime evaluation specifies an A6000 GPU, 202k primitives, and 1100x1604 rendering. The original four-subject splits, metrics, and training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds quantitative and qualitative tests isolating neural diffuse shading versus PRT and Cook-Torrance specular shading versus spherical Gaussians. Appendix C also compares full and restricted camera configurations. These substantially extend the component and camera-count analyses; the intrinsic-decomposition comparison already existed in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new tables continue reporting point estimates; randomly selected camera and lighting subsets do not establish repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the existing Table 3 entries are unchanged, but substantial results are added. SG achieves relighting PSNR 31.55 versus 31.38 for the full model. Table 4 reports 17 ms for BecomingLit versus 20 ms for RGCA. Goliath results favor BecomingLit on SSIM and LPIPS but favor RGCA on PSNR in both camera configurations; full-camera PSNR is 29.70 versus 29.89. These are new comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix B rendering derivation are retained. Renaming specular intensity from s to k_s, simplifying subscripts, and making viewing-direction dependence explicit do not change the mathematics. No new theorem, assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an economical OLAT capture dataset and a relightable Gaussian avatar using hybrid neural shading, with interactive rendering and monocular-video animation. The added experiments support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 discusses PRT's generalization difficulties and justifies retaining Cook-Torrance for natural pore-level reflections despite SG's slightly better PSNR and LPIPS. It adds specific gaze-tracking, mouth-interior, and uncalibrated phone-capture limitations, and attributes differences from previously published Goliath imagery to subsampling and compression.

D1.justification: Section 4.5 changes the reported training GPU from RTX 3090 to RTX A6000 while retaining approximately 30 hours of training. v2 removes the statement that the normal-loss weight decays from 1 to 0 over 200k iterations, reducing reproducibility without establishing a changed schedule. New runtime and Goliath details are supplied; network specifications and data-access restrictions remain.

R1.justification: New Section 4.6 provides a focused architectural comparison with RGCA's personalized variational autoencoder and PRT representation, clarifying the role of shared FLAME conditioning and hybrid shading. This modestly expands positioning against the closest prior method; the same 57 references are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and notation edits, adds dedicated RGCA-comparison and runtime subsections, and reorganizes Appendix C around Goliath. Intrinsic-decomposition discussion moves into the main results. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The results displays are substantially expanded and reorganized. v1's appendix decomposition comparison is incorporated into main Figure 5 with a ground-truth column; Figure 6 and Table 3 gain PRT and SG comparisons. New Table 4 presents runtime, while appendix Figure 8 and Table 5 present Goliath results. Several other figures retain identical imagery.

improvement.justification: The added shading controls, external-dataset evaluation, and measured runtime strengthen support for the existing modeling and practicality claims. More specific limitations improve interpretation. The net gain is limited by the single-subject Goliath evaluation and partly offset by deletion of the normal-loss decay schedule, which weakens reproducibility.
